name: OpenGenes_get_gene
description: Get the aging/longevity profile of a human gene by symbol from Open Genes, a manually-curated aging-gene database. Returns the gene's aging mechanisms (e.g. INS/IGF-1 pathway dysregulation), functional clusters, associated disease categories, curator confidence level, expression change with age, and an evidence-count summary across study types (lifespan-increase studies, longevity associations, age-related changes, progeria associations, interventions). Use to assess whether and how a gene is implicated in aging. No API key required.

oneOf.description: The gene's aging profile. This branch declared no properties at all, so none of the fourteen fields the tool returns was discoverable from the schema.

evidence_counts.description: How many records of each evidence type; see evidence_summary for what they say

evidence_summary.description: Per evidence type, what the records actually say: the distinct longevity effects, intervention results, change types, model organisms and ethnicities, plus the DOIs. GHR has 57 longevity associations and 14 lifespan studies, and the tool reported '57' and '14' -- counts, for a tool whose description says to use it to assess whether and HOW a gene is implicated in aging, with no other tool in the family returning the records.

name: OpenGenes_search_genes
description: Browse the complete Open Genes catalog of human aging/longevity genes with one-based page pagination and pages up to 1000 records. Metadata reports the exact gene count, total_pages, has_more, and next_page. Returns gene summaries with aging mechanisms, functional clusters, confidence level, and expression change. No API key required.

page.description: One-based page number (default 1). Continue with metadata.next_page.
